chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durost, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

In the Siwak (brushing teeth with a twig) there are twelve characteristics: It is from the Sunnah, it purifies the mouth, it clarifies the vision, it pleases the Merciful, it whitens the teeth, it removes the hollows (or bad breath), it strengthens the gums, it stimulates the appetite, it removes the phlegm, it increases memory, it multiplies the good deeds, and the angels rejoice in it.

key_terms.الرَّحْمَان: The Merciful, one of the names of God
key_terms.السُّنَّة: The prophetic tradition or recommended practice
key_terms.السِّوَاك: Brushing teeth with a twig, a prophetic practice for oral hygiene

ai.seo_question: What are the twelve spiritual and physical benefits of using the Siwak according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines twelve specific virtues of the Siwak, blending physical hygiene with spiritual purification to demonstrate the holistic nature of Shia jurisprudence. This enumeration underscores the practice not merely as a personal habit but as a means of attracting divine pleasure and angelic delight, reinforcing its status as a confirmed Sunnah. The text reflects the scholarly tradition of linking bodily care with spiritual elevation, a theme prevalent in Imami hadith literature.
